text_blocks.snippet: Common scams actively targeting residents across Central Illinois include fake government text alerts, pre-trial release demands, and fraudulent package delivery notifications. Scammers frequently use artificial intelligence and local data to make these requests look and sound authentic.
snippet_highlighted_words: fake government text alerts, pre-trial release demands, and fraudulent package delivery notifications

text_blocks.snippet: Active Scam Types in Central Illinois

list.snippet: Fake Traffic & Toll Violations: Text messages claiming to be from the Illinois Secretary of State, IDOT, or tollway services threaten immediate license suspension or legal action if you do not click a link to pay an overdue fine. State agencies never request payments via text.

Pre-Trial Release Scams: Con artists contact family members of individuals in local justice systems, posing as pre-trial services or court officials and demanding immediate cash (via apps like Zelle or Cash App) to secure a relative's release or GPS monitoring.
Package Delivery Texts: Phishing texts claiming a package is held by the USPS or UPS ask for personal data or small fee payments to update a missing delivery address.
Pen Pal & Relationship Scams: Unsolicited messages mirror your personal interests on social media or text, eventually steering you to alternate apps before asking for gift cards or cash assistance.
AI-Driven Impostor Calls: Scammers use voice cloning or urgent family/celebrity impersonation to trick older adults into wiring money under false emergencies.
Practice the Pause: Take a step back when a message or call demands immediate action, secrecy, or panic.
Never Click Links: Do not tap on links in unexpected text messages or emails regarding fines, tolls, or packages.
Verify Independently: Hang up and call official numbers directly (like a family member or a verified agency line) rather than dialing numbers provided in suspicious messages.
Report Fraud: File local reports or check active alerts through the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois or report state text scams directly to the official Illinois Scam Alert site.
